source.text: Ταῦτα ἐν παροιμίαις λελάληκα ὑμῖν· ἔρχεται ὥρα ὅτε οὐκέτι ἐν παροιμίαις λαλήσω ὑμῖν ἀλλὰ παρρησίᾳ περὶ τοῦ πατρὸς ἀπαγγελῶ ὑμῖν.

records.literal_gloss: "These things in figures of speech I have spoken to you; is coming an hour when no longer in figures of speech I will speak to you, but plainly concerning the Father I will report to you.

en.L: "These things I have spoken to you in figures of speech. An hour is coming when I will no longer speak to you in figures of speech, but I will report to you plainly about the Father.
en.B: "I have used figures of speech in telling you these things. An hour is coming when I will no longer use them with you; I will tell you about the Father in plain words.
en.R: "I have been telling you these things in pictures. But an hour is coming when I will stop speaking to you in pictures. Then I will tell you clearly about the Father.

fr.L: « Ces choses, je vous les ai dites en paroles figurées ; une heure vient où je ne vous parlerai plus en paroles figurées, mais je vous annoncerai ouvertement [ce qui concerne] le Père.
fr.B: « Je vous ai dit cela en langage figuré. Une heure vient où je ne vous parlerai plus ainsi : je vous parlerai du Père en termes clairs.
fr.R: « Je vous ai dit tout cela avec des images. Mais l’heure vient où je ne vous parlerai plus avec des images. Alors je vous parlerai clairement du Père.

vi.L: "Những điều này {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã nói với các con bằng lời bóng gió. Giờ đang đến khi {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ không còn nói với các con bằng lời bóng gió nữa, nhưng sẽ nói rõ cho các con biết về Cha.
vi.B: "Ta đã dùng lời bóng gió mà nói với các con những điều này. Giờ đang đến khi {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ không dùng lời bóng gió với các con nữa, nhưng sẽ nói thẳng cho các con về Cha.
vi.R: "Ta đã nói với các con những điều này bằng hình ảnh. Nhưng giờ đang đến khi {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ thôi nói với các con bằng hình ảnh. Khi ấy {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ nói rõ ràng cho các con về Cha.

ko.L: "내가 이것들을 비유로 너희에게 말하였다. 내가 더 이상 비유로 너희에게 말하지 않고, 아버지에 대하여 밝히 너희에게 전할 때가 온다.
ko.B: "나는 이것을 비유로 너희에게 말하였다. 그러나 내가 더 이상 비유를 쓰지 않고, 아버지에 대하여 분명한 말로 너희에게 알려 줄 때가 온다.
ko.R: "지금까지는 내가 이런 것들을 빗대어 말했다. 그러나 이제 더 이상 빗대어 말하지 않을 때가 온다. 그때에는 아버지에 대해 너희에게 분명하게 말해 줄 것이다.

decisions.choice: figures of speech: veiled sayings whose meaning has to be worked out
alternatives: parables in the sense of the stories in the other Gospels
decisions.reason: The same word described the picture of the shepherd and the sheep (10:6). Here it covers the images of the farewell talk: the Father's house with many rooms (14:2), the vine and the branches (15:1-8), the woman in labor (16:21), and the sayings about going away and coming back after "a little while" (16:16-19), which the disciples could not understand.

decisions.choice: plainly: in clear, direct words, without figures
decisions.reason: The word can mean speaking in public (7:26) or speaking with confidence, but here it is set against figures of speech, as in 10:24 and 11:14, so it means plain speech. The disciples pick up the same two words in 16:29.

decisions.choice: the coming hour: the time after Jesus's death and return to the Father, when the Spirit teaches them
alternatives: the rest of this same conversation
the hour of his death only
decisions.reason: Jesus has said that the Spirit will teach them everything and remind them of what he said (14:26) and guide them into all the truth (16:13); after the resurrection they understood what they had not understood before (2:22; 12:16). The "day" of 16:23 and 16:26 is the same time. In 16:29 the disciples think this hour has already arrived, and Jesus's answer (16:31-32) shows that it has not.

decisions.choice: report: announce, bring word
decisions.reason: The verb is used of bringing news or a message (4:51; 1 John 1:2-3). Jesus will make the Father known openly, as the one who has come from him (1:18).

decisions.choice: figures of speech (L, B), pictures (R); plainly (L), in plain words (B), clearly (R)
decisions.reason: The same English as 10:6 for the figure of speech and 10:24 for plainly, so that readers can follow John's thread from those chapters to 16:29. Readable uses the plain words it used there.

decisions.choice: hour, at every level
decisions.reason: As elsewhere in John (12:23; 13:1), "hour" is kept at every level so that the thread of Jesus's appointed time stays visible. The Greek has no article, so the English says "an hour", as in 4:21 and 5:25.

decisions.choice: en paroles figurées (L), en langage figuré (B), avec des images (R); ouvertement (L), en termes clairs (B), clairement (R)
decisions.reason: The word means veiled sayings whose sense has to be worked out (meaning decision m1), not the story-parables of the other Gospels, so French avoids "paraboles". Each level keeps its pair of words in verse 29, where the disciples answer with the same two Greek words.

decisions.choice: une heure vient (L, B); l’heure vient (R)
decisions.reason: As the English, "heure" is kept at every level so that the thread of Jesus's hour stays visible (meaning decision m3; again in verse 32). Readable says "l’heure vient", which is ordinary French for a time drawing near.

decisions.choice: lời bóng gió (L, B); hình ảnh (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek word is a veiled saying whose meaning has to be worked out. "Lời bóng gió" is speech that hints rather than says; "ẩn dụ" (metaphor) is a grammar term, and "ví dụ" today means "example".

decisions.choice: Jesus says "Ta" for himself and "các con" to the disciples
decisions.reason: The forms of address the style guide sets for the whole book, recorded once in this passage. The disciples answer him as "Thầy" and call themselves "chúng con" (verses 29-30).

decisions.choice: 비유 (L, B); 빗대어 말하다 (R) for "figures of speech"; 밝히 (L), 분명한 말로 (B), 분명하게 (R) for "plainly"
decisions.reason: 비유 is the ordinary word for a veiled saying; Readable says the same with a verb new readers know.

source.text: ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἐν τῷ ὀνόματί μου αἰτήσεσθε, καὶ οὐ λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι ἐγὼ ἐρωτήσω τὸν πατέρα περὶ ὑμῶν·

records.literal_gloss: In that the day in the name of me you will ask, and not I say to you that I will ask the Father concerning you;

en.L: In that day you will ask in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name, and I do not say to you that I will ask the Father concerning you;
en.B: On that day you will ask in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name, and I do not say that I will ask the Father on your behalf.
en.R: When that day comes, you will make your requests in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name. And I am not saying that I myself will ask the Father for you.

fr.L: En ce jour-là, vous demanderez en {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom, et je ne vous dis pas que {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, je prierai le Père à votre sujet ;
fr.B: Ce jour-là, vous demanderez en {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom, et je ne dis pas que je prierai le Père en votre faveur.
fr.R: Quand ce jour-là viendra, vous ferez vos demandes en {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom. Et je ne dis pas que c’est {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} qui prierai le Père pour vous.

vi.L: Trong ngày đó các con sẽ xin trong danh {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} không nói với các con rằng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ cầu xin Cha cho các con;
vi.B: Trong ngày đó, các con sẽ xin trong danh {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} không nói rằng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ thay các con mà cầu xin Cha.
vi.R: Đến ngày đó, các con sẽ xin trong danh {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} không nói rằng chính {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ xin Cha giùm các con.

ko.L: 그날에 너희는 내 이름으로 구할 것이다. 그리고 내가 너희를 위하여 아버지께 청하겠다고 너희에게 말하지 않는다.
ko.B: 그날에는 너희가 내 이름으로 구할 것이다. 내가 너희를 위하여 아버지께 청하겠다고 말하지 않는다.
ko.R: 그날이 오면 너희가 내 이름으로 구할 것이다. 내가 너희를 위해 아버지께 대신 구해 주겠다고 말하는 것이 아니다.

decisions.choice: in that day: the time after the resurrection, the coming hour of 16:25
decisions.reason: The phrase points back to 16:23 and to 14:20, "In that day you will know that I am in my Father". It is the time after Jesus has gone to the Father and has come back to them, not the end of the age.

decisions.choice: ask in my name: ask the Father as people who belong to Jesus, on his authority
alternatives: use Jesus's name as a formula
decisions.reason: As in 14:13-14 and 16:23-24, asking in Jesus's name means coming to the Father as his disciples, in keeping with who he is. The verb here is the ordinary word for making a request.

decisions.choice: not a denial that Jesus prays for them, but a statement that the Father needs no persuading
alternatives: Jesus will no longer pray for his disciples
decisions.reason: Jesus does pray for them, in the very next chapter (17:9, 15, 20), and elsewhere the New Testament speaks of him interceding for his people (Romans 8:34; 1 John 2:1). The point here is the reason Jesus gives at once: the Father himself loves them (16:27). They will not need a go-between to win over a reluctant Father.

decisions.choice: ask: make a request on someone's behalf
decisions.reason: This verb can mean to ask a question (16:19, 23, 30) or to make a request (14:16; 17:9). With "concerning you" it is a request: speaking to the Father for them.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}}, {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}
decisions.reason: Every pronoun for Jesus or for the Father uses the deity_pronoun setting, including "me" and "my" when Jesus speaks of himself and "you" when the disciples speak to him (16:29-30). At the start of a sentence the pronoun is written plain. This applies throughout 16:25-33.

decisions.choice: on your behalf (B), for you (R)
decisions.reason: "Concerning you" is word for word; with a verb of asking it means speaking for them, so Balanced and Readable say so.

decisions.choice: demander (the disciples' requests); prier le Père (Jesus asking on their behalf)
decisions.reason: Two verbs again (meaning decisions m2 and m4). French "prier quelqu’un pour quelqu’un" is the natural way to say that Jesus asks the Father on their behalf, and it is the verb used for his prayer for them in 17:9, 15 and 20.

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in Korean
alternatives: capitalised pronoun spans as in English
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters, so the deity_pronoun setting has nothing to change; respect is carried by the honorific -si-, 께서 and 그분 at every level (style guide section 7).

decisions.choice: 청하다 (L, B) for Jesus asking the Father; 구하다 for the disciples' asking
decisions.reason: 청하다 is a request made on someone's behalf; it keeps the second Greek verb apart from the disciples' 구하다.

source.text: αὐτὸς γὰρ ὁ πατὴρ φιλεῖ ὑμᾶς, ὅτι ὑμεῖς ἐμὲ πεφιλήκατε καὶ πεπιστεύκατε ὅτι ἐγὼ παρὰ τοῦ θεοῦ ἐξῆλθον.

records.literal_gloss: Himself for the Father loves you, because you me have loved and have believed that I from the God came out.

en.L: for the Father {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} loves you, because you have loved {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and have believed that I came out from God.
en.B: For the Father {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} loves you, since you have loved {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and believed that I came out from God.
en.R: The Father {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} loves you. He loves you because you have come to love {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and to believe that I came from God.

fr.L: car le Père {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}} vous aime, parce que vous {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}avez aimé et que vous avez cru que {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, je suis sorti d’auprès de Dieu.
fr.B: En effet, le Père {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}} vous aime, puisque vous {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}avez aimé et que vous avez cru que je suis venu d’auprès de Dieu.
fr.R: Le Père {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}} vous aime. Il vous aime parce que vous vous êtes mis à {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}aimer et à croire que je viens de Dieu.

vi.L: vì chính Cha yêu các con, bởi các con đã yêu {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} và đã tin rằng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã ra từ Đức Chúa Trời.
vi.B: Vì chính Cha yêu các con, bởi các con đã yêu {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} và tin rằng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} từ Đức Chúa Trời mà ra.
vi.R: Chính Cha yêu các con. Cha yêu các con vì các con đã yêu {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} và tin rằng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đến từ Đức Chúa Trời.

ko.L: 아버지께서 친히 너희를 사랑하시기 때문이다. 이는 너희가 나를 사랑하였고 내가 하나님께로부터 나왔다는 것을 믿었기 때문이다.
ko.B: 아버지께서 몸소 너희를 사랑하시기 때문이다. 너희가 나를 사랑하였고, 내가 하나님께로부터 나온 것을 믿었기 때문이다.
ko.R: 아버지께서 직접 너희를 사랑하신다. 너희가 나를 사랑하게 되었고, 내가 하나님께로부터 왔다는 것을 믿게 되었기 때문이다.

decisions.choice: love: the same love as elsewhere in John, though the verb differs
alternatives: a warmer or lesser love of friendship, set against another verb for love
decisions.reason: John has two verbs for love and uses both of the Father's love for the Son (3:35; 5:20). Here he uses the one often linked with friendship, both for the Father's love and for the disciples' love of Jesus. The thought is the same as 14:21 and 14:23, where the other verb is used: the Father loves those who love the Son.

decisions.choice: the Father himself: of his own accord, without being persuaded
alternatives: the Father as well as Jesus
decisions.reason: The pronoun stands first for emphasis and answers 16:26: Jesus need not ask the Father for them, because the Father himself already loves them.

decisions.choice: because: their love and belief are the ground on which the Father's love meets them, not a payment that earns it
alternatives: the Father began to love them only when they loved Jesus
decisions.reason: The two verbs are perfect tenses: they have come to love Jesus and to believe, and they still do. John says elsewhere that God loved the world first (3:16; 1 John 4:10, 19). What is said here is that those who receive the Son are loved by the Father as the Son's own (14:21, 23; 17:23).

decisions.choice: from God, as in the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Some early and important manuscripts read "from the Father", which matches the next verse; others, also early, read "from God", which the SBLGNT follows. Copyists could easily have brought this verse into line with 16:28. The sense is the same either way. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: came out from (L, B), came from (R)
decisions.reason: The verb means to go out or come out; Literal and Balanced say "came out from" as in 8:42, so that readers see the picture of coming out from the Father's presence. Readable says it simply.

decisions.choice: The Father himself loves you. He loves you because ...
alternatives: For the Father himself loves you, because ...
decisions.reason: Readable begins a new sentence and repeats "he loves you" so that the reason can stand on its own. The link with 16:26 is still clear from the order of the sentences. "Have come to love ... and to believe" brings out the perfect tenses (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: sortir (L); venir (B, R), here and in verses 28 and 30
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the picture of the verb, "come out", as the English does. In ordinary French "je suis sorti de Dieu" sounds odd, so Balanced and Readable say "venir de", which carries the same sense of where Jesus comes from (meaning decision m4); Balanced keeps "d’auprès de" for the preposition that means "from beside".

decisions.choice: chính Cha, with no setting span
decisions.reason: The English "the Father himself" has a pronoun under the setting. Vietnamese gives the emphasis with "chính" (the very one) before "Cha", a capitalised noun, so no pronoun or setting is needed.

source.text: ἐξῆλθον ἐκ τοῦ πατρὸς καὶ ἐλήλυθα εἰς τὸν κόσμον· πάλιν ἀφίημι τὸν κόσμον καὶ πορεύομαι πρὸς τὸν πατέρα.

records.literal_gloss: I came out from the Father and have come into the world; again I leave the world and go to the Father."

en.L: I came out from the Father and have come into the world; again, I am leaving the world and going to the Father."
en.B: I came out from the Father and have come into the world. Now, in turn, I am leaving the world and going to the Father."
en.R: I came from the Father and came into the world. Now I am leaving the world and going back to the Father."

fr.L: Je suis sorti du Père et je suis venu dans le monde ; de nouveau, je quitte le monde et je vais vers le Père. »
fr.B: Je suis venu d’auprès du Père et je suis entré dans le monde. Maintenant, je fais le chemin inverse : je quitte le monde et je vais vers le Père. »
fr.R: Je suis venu du Père, et je suis arrivé dans le monde. Maintenant, je quitte le monde et je retourne auprès du Père. »

vi.L: Ta đã ra từ Cha và đã đến trong thế gian; lại nữa, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} lìa thế gian và đi đến cùng Cha."
vi.B: Ta đã ra từ Cha và đã đến thế gian. Giờ đây, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} lại rời thế gian mà đi về cùng Cha."
vi.R: Ta từ Cha mà đến, và đã vào thế gian. Bây giờ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} rời thế gian và trở về với Cha."

ko.L: 내가 아버지께로부터 나와서 세상에 왔다. 다시 내가 세상을 떠나 아버지께로 간다."
ko.B: 나는 아버지께로부터 나와서 세상에 왔다. 이제 다시 세상을 떠나 아버지께로 간다."
ko.R: 나는 아버지께로부터 세상에 왔다. 이제는 세상을 떠나 아버지께로 돌아간다."

decisions.choice: the first clause, "I came out from the Father", is part of the text, as in the SBLGNT
alternatives: the verse begins "and I have come into the world"
decisions.reason: Codex Bezae and a few other witnesses, including some Old Latin manuscripts, lack the first clause. Most manuscripts have it. Copyists may have left it out because it seemed to repeat the end of 16:27. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: again: in turn, going back the way he came
decisions.reason: Jesus is not leaving the world for a second time. "Again" marks the reverse movement: he came from the Father into the world, and now he leaves the world for the Father. The verse sums up the whole Gospel (1:1, 14; 13:1, 3).

decisions.choice: I leave, I go: the present tense for a departure already under way
decisions.reason: The departure is still ahead, but Jesus speaks of it as already happening, as in 14:28 and 16:5. The hour has come (13:1).

decisions.choice: the world: the human world into which the Son came
alternatives: the world as hostile to God
decisions.reason: Here the world is the place and people to whom the Son was sent (1:9-10; 3:17), not, as in 16:33, humanity set against God. World is a key term.

decisions.choice: Now, in turn (B); going back (R)
decisions.reason: "Again" could be read as a second departure; Balanced and Readable give the sense of reversing the journey (meaning decision m2). Balanced and Readable add "now" for the change from his coming to his going.

decisions.choice: I am leaving ... going
decisions.reason: The English progressive shows a departure that is about to happen and has in a sense begun (meaning decision m3).

source.text: Λέγουσιν οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ· Ἴδε νῦν ἐν παρρησίᾳ λαλεῖς, καὶ παροιμίαν οὐδεμίαν λέγεις.

records.literal_gloss: Say the disciples of him, "Look, now in plainness you speak, and figure of speech none you say.

en.L: His disciples say, "Look, now {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are speaking plainly, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are saying no figure of speech.
en.B: His disciples said, "Look, now {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are speaking in plain words and not using any figure of speech!
en.R: Then {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples said, "Now {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are speaking clearly! You are not using pictures anymore.

fr.L: Ses disciples disent : « Voilà que maintenant {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} parles ouvertement, et {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} ne dis aucune parole figurée.
fr.B: Ses disciples dirent : « Voilà, maintenant {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} parles en termes clairs, sans aucun langage figuré !
fr.R: Alors {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples ont dit : « Maintenant, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} parles clairement ! Tu n’utilises plus d’images.

vi.L: Các môn đồ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói: "Kìa, bây giờ Thầy nói rõ ràng, và không nói lời bóng gió nào cả.
vi.B: Các môn đồ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} thưa: "Kìa, bây giờ Thầy nói rõ ràng, chứ không dùng lời bóng gió nào nữa!
vi.R: Bấy giờ các môn đồ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} thưa: "Bây giờ Thầy nói rõ ràng rồi! Thầy không còn dùng hình ảnh nữa.

ko.L: 그분의 제자들이 말한다. "보십시오, 이제 밝히 말씀하시고 비유는 하나도 말씀하지 않으십니다.
ko.B: 제자들이 말했다. "보십시오, 이제 분명한 말로 말씀하시고 비유는 전혀 쓰지 않으십니다!
ko.R: 그러자 제자들이 말했다. "이제는 분명하게 말씀하십니다! 더 이상 빗대어 말씀하지 않으십니다.

decisions.choice: the disciples think the promised hour of plain speech has already come
alternatives: they rightly see that Jesus has now spoken plainly
decisions.reason: Jesus said that an hour is coming when he will speak plainly (16:25); the disciples answer "now". Jesus has indeed said something direct (16:28), but his reply (16:31-32) shows that they have not yet understood what is about to happen. Their "now" is said too soon.

decisions.choice: plainly and figure of speech: the same two words as 16:25
decisions.reason: The disciples repeat Jesus's words, setting plain speech against figures, as in 10:6 and 10:24.

decisions.choice: look: a call to attention
alternatives: see, an order to look at something
decisions.reason: The word draws attention to what they think has just happened. It does not ask anyone to see something with the eyes.

decisions.choice: Historic present: say (L); said (B, R)
decisions.reason: John tells this past event in the present tense ("his disciples say") to make it vivid. Literal keeps the present so that readers see the Greek form; Balanced and Readable use the past, the normal tense for telling a story in English. This decision applies to the historic present in 16:25-33.

decisions.choice: plainly (L), in plain words (B), clearly (R); figure of speech (L, B), pictures (R)
decisions.reason: The same English as in 16:25, so that readers hear the disciples repeat Jesus's words.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B), with Literal keeping John's present tense ("ses disciples disent"); passé composé (R); speech in the passé composé at every level
alternatives: passé composé for narration at every level
decisions.reason: The French brief for the passage (16:25-33), as in 1:19. Literal keeps the historic present where John uses it, as the English Literal does; Balanced narrates in the passé simple ("dirent", "répondit"), the tense of written narrative; Readable uses the passé composé ("ont dit"). Inside speech every level uses the passé composé ("je vous ai dit", "j’ai vaincu").

decisions.choice: Thầy for "you"; thưa (B, R)
decisions.reason: The disciples address Jesus as "Thầy" (Teacher) and speak of themselves as "chúng con", as the style guide sets; "Thầy" is a capitalised noun and takes no setting, where the English "you" has one. Balanced and Readable use "thưa", the respectful verb for speaking to a superior; Literal keeps the plain "nói" in the historic present.

decisions.choice: Historic present kept at Literal (말한다); past at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: John tells this in the present; Literal keeps it, Balanced and Readable use the narrative past (one decision for the passage).

decisions.choice: The disciples speak to Jesus in the formal polite style (합쇼체), with no pronoun for "you"
decisions.reason: Disciples address Jesus in 합쇼체 (style guide section 4); Korean does not say 당신 to a teacher, and the honorific verb already shows who is meant.

source.text: νῦν οἴδαμεν ὅτι οἶδας πάντα καὶ οὐ χρείαν ἔχεις ἵνα τίς σε ἐρωτᾷ· ἐν τούτῳ πιστεύομεν ὅτι ἀπὸ θεοῦ ἐξῆλθες.

records.literal_gloss: Now we know that you know all things and not need you have that anyone you should question; by this we believe that from God you came out."

en.L: Now we know that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} know all things and have no need that anyone question {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; by this we believe that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} came out from God."
en.B: Now we know that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} know all things and do not need anyone to put questions to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. This is why we believe that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} came out from God."
en.R: Now we know that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} know everything. You do not need anyone to ask {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} questions. That is why we believe that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} came from God."

fr.L: Maintenant nous savons que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} sais toutes choses et que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} n’as pas besoin que quelqu’un {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}interroge ; par là, nous croyons que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} es sorti de Dieu. »
fr.B: Maintenant nous savons que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} sais tout et que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} n’as pas besoin qu’on {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} pose des questions. Voilà pourquoi nous croyons que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} es venu de Dieu. »
fr.R: Maintenant nous savons que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} sais tout. Tu n’as pas besoin qu’on {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} pose des questions. C’est pour cela que nous croyons que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} es venu de Dieu. »

vi.L: Bây giờ chúng con biết rằng Thầy biết mọi điều và không cần ai hỏi Thầy; bởi điều này chúng con tin rằng Thầy đã ra từ Đức Chúa Trời."
vi.B: Bây giờ chúng con biết Thầy biết hết mọi sự, không cần ai phải hỏi Thầy. Vì thế chúng con tin Thầy từ Đức Chúa Trời mà ra."
vi.R: Bây giờ chúng con biết Thầy biết hết mọi điều. Thầy không cần ai hỏi Thầy cả. Vì vậy chúng con tin rằng Thầy đến từ Đức Chúa Trời."

ko.L: 이제 우리는, 모든 것을 아시고 누가 여쭐 필요도 없으시다는 것을 압니다. 이것으로 우리는 하나님께로부터 나오신 것을 믿습니다."
ko.B: 이제 우리는 주님께서 모든 것을 아시며, 아무도 주님께 여쭈어 볼 필요가 없다는 것을 압니다. 그래서 우리는 주님께서 하나님께로부터 나오신 것을 믿습니다."
ko.R: 이제 우리는 주님께서 모든 것을 아신다는 것을 알겠습니다. 누가 주님께 물어볼 필요도 없습니다. 그래서 우리는 주님께서 하나님께로부터 오신 것을 믿습니다."

decisions.choice: no need that anyone question you: Jesus knows their questions before they ask them
alternatives: no need for anyone to teach you
decisions.reason: Jesus answered the question they wanted to ask (16:17-19) before they put it to him. He knows what is in people (2:24-25; 1:48). The disciples take this as proof that he knows all things.

decisions.choice: question: ask questions of someone
decisions.reason: The same verb meant making a request in 16:26; here, as in 16:19 and 16:23, it means asking questions.

decisions.choice: by this: because of this, on this ground
alternatives: in this, in the sense of in this matter
decisions.reason: "This" is Jesus's knowledge of their thoughts. It is the reason they give for believing.

decisions.choice: a true confession, but not yet a full understanding
decisions.reason: They say what Jesus said in 16:27, and it is true (17:8). But they believe on the strength of what they have just seen, and Jesus's next words test it (16:31-32).

decisions.choice: This is why (B); That is why (R)
decisions.reason: "In this" or "by this" is word for word; Balanced and Readable give the causal sense plainly (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: 주님 for "you" addressed to Jesus (B, R); Literal leaves the subject to the honorific verb
decisions.reason: The disciples are confessing faith, so 주님 fits; Korean avoids a second-person pronoun to a superior, and Literal follows the Greek, which has no separate word for most of these "you"s.

records.literal_gloss: Answered them Jesus, "Now do you believe?

en.L: Jesus answered them, "Now do you believe?
en.B: Jesus answered them, "Do you believe now?
en.R: Jesus answered them, "Do you believe now?

fr.L: Jésus leur répondit : « À présent vous croyez ?
fr.B: Jésus leur répondit : « Vous croyez, maintenant ?
fr.R: Jésus leur a répondu : « Alors maintenant, vous croyez ?

vi.L: Đức Giê-xu đáp lại họ: "Bây giờ các con tin sao?
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu trả lời họ: "Giờ các con tin rồi sao?
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu trả lời họ: "Bây giờ các con tin rồi à?

decisions.choice: a question, as the SBLGNT punctuates it
decisions.reason: The Greek has no punctuation of its own, and the words could be a question or a statement. Taken as a question, Jesus asks whether their belief is as firm as they think. Taken as a statement, he grants that they believe, and the next verse shows how soon it will be tested. Either way the following words are a warning, not a rejection: he goes on to promise them peace (16:33).

decisions.choice: now: at this moment, picking up the disciples' own "now"
decisions.reason: The disciples twice said "now" (16:29, 30). Jesus's word, placed first, takes it up: at this very point, when the hour of their scattering is about to come (16:32).

decisions.choice: a testing of their belief, not a denial that they believe
alternatives: Jesus dismisses their belief as false
decisions.reason: Jesus answered Peter's promise in the same way (13:37-38). He has just said that they have believed (16:27); what he questions is whether they understand what is coming.

decisions.choice: Do you believe now?
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "now" first, as in the Greek. Balanced and Readable use ordinary English order; a reader aloud can still stress "now".

source.text: ἰδοὺ ἔρχεται ὥρα καὶ ἐλήλυθεν ἵνα σκορπισθῆτε ἕκαστος εἰς τὰ ἴδια κἀμὲ μόνον ἀφῆτε· καὶ οὐκ εἰμὶ μόνος, ὅτι ὁ πατὴρ μετ’ ἐμοῦ ἐστιν.

records.literal_gloss: Look, is coming an hour and has come that you be scattered each to the own [things] and me alone you leave; and not I am alone, because the Father with me is.

en.L: Look, an hour is coming and has come, when you will be scattered, each to his own [home], and will leave {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} alone; and I am not alone, because the Father is with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.B: Look, an hour is coming, and in fact has come, when you will be scattered, each to his own home, and will leave {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} alone. Yet I am not alone, for the Father is with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.R: Look, an hour is coming, and it is already here, when you will all run off, each to his own home. You will leave {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} all alone. But I am not alone. The Father is with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

fr.L: Voici qu’une heure vient, et elle est venue, où vous serez dispersés, chacun chez soi, et vous {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} laisserez seul ; et je ne suis pas seul, parce que le Père est avec {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}.
fr.B: Voici qu’une heure vient, et en fait elle est là, où vous serez dispersés, chacun rentrant chez lui, et vous {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} laisserez seul. Pourtant je ne suis pas seul, car le Père est avec {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}.
fr.R: Écoutez : l’heure vient, et elle est déjà là, où vous allez tous partir en courant, chacun chez soi. Vous {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} laisserez tout seul. Mais je ne suis pas seul. Le Père est avec {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}.

vi.L: Kìa, giờ đang đến và đã đến rồi, khi các con sẽ bị tản lạc, mỗi người về [nhà] riêng mình, và để {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} lại một mình; nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} không một mình, vì Cha ở với {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.
vi.B: Kìa, giờ đang đến, và thật ra đã đến rồi, khi các con bị tản lạc, ai về nhà nấy, bỏ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} lại một mình. Nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} không ở một mình, vì Cha ở với {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.
vi.R: Kìa, giờ đang đến, và đã đến rồi, khi các con sẽ bỏ chạy tán loạn, ai về nhà nấy. Các con sẽ để {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} lại một mình. Nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} không một mình đâu. Cha ở với {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.

ko.L: 보라, 너희가 각각 자기 [집으로] 흩어지고 나를 혼자 버려둘 때가 오고 있고, 이미 왔다. 그러나 나는 혼자가 아니다. 아버지께서 나와 함께 계시기 때문이다.
ko.B: 보아라, 너희가 각자 제집으로 흩어지고 나를 홀로 남겨 둘 때가 오고 있다. 아니, 이미 왔다. 그러나 나는 혼자가 아니다. 아버지께서 나와 함께 계시기 때문이다.
ko.R: 잘 들어라. 너희가 모두 뿔뿔이 흩어져 저마다 자기 집으로 달아날 때가 오고 있다. 아니, 벌써 왔다. 너희는 나를 혼자 남겨 둘 것이다. 그러나 나는 혼자가 아니다. 아버지께서 나와 함께 계신다.

decisions.choice: the hour: Jesus's hour, the time of his arrest and death, now arriving
decisions.reason: "Is coming and has come" is said as in 4:23 and 5:25. This is the hour of 12:23, 12:27 and 13:1, so near that it has in effect begun; that same night the disciples will scatter at his arrest.

decisions.choice: an echo of Zechariah 13:7, the shepherd struck and the sheep scattered
alternatives: no allusion; scattered is simply the natural word
decisions.reason: In Mark 14:27 and Matthew 26:31 Jesus quotes Zechariah 13:7, "Strike the shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered", on the same night. John does not quote it, but he uses the same verb for scattering, and he has used it of the wolf scattering the sheep (10:12). The echo is likely but not certain.

decisions.choice: each to his own: each one going off to his own home or his own place
alternatives: each back to his own former life
decisions.reason: The phrase, "to the own things", means one's own home or place, as in 19:27, where the disciple takes Jesus's mother "to his own". It pictures the group breaking up as each one goes his own way.

decisions.choice: Jesus is not alone, because the Father is with him even when the disciples leave
decisions.reason: Jesus said the same in 8:16 and 8:29, "The one who sent me is with me; he has not left me alone." The "and" here has the force of "yet": the disciples will leave him, but the Father will not.

decisions.choice: each to his own [home] (L); each to his own home (B, R)
alternatives: each to their own home (under the gender setting)
decisions.reason: Jesus is speaking to the eleven disciples, specific men, so "his" is plain and takes no gender setting (style guide, section 6). Literal brackets "home", which the Greek leaves understood ("to his own things").

decisions.choice: [home] (L); home (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek says only "his own" with a plural article ("the own things"); English needs a noun, and "home" gives the sense of meaning decision m3. Readable says "run off" for the scattering, which is what they did at the arrest.

decisions.choice: chacun chez soi
alternatives: chacun vers [ce qui est à lui]
decisions.reason: The Greek says "each to his own" without a noun (meaning decision m3). French "chez soi" says "to one's own home" in two words, so Literal needs no bracket where the English supplies "[home]"; "de son côté" would lose the sense of going home.

decisions.choice: The "when" clause comes before 때 (hour) in Korean; "and has come" follows as its own clause (이미 왔다)
alternatives: keeping "is coming and has come" together before the clause
decisions.reason: A Korean relative clause precedes its noun, so the scattering is told first and the double "coming / has come" closes the sentence.

source.text: ταῦτα λελάληκα ὑμῖν ἵνα ἐν ἐμοὶ εἰρήνην ἔχητε· ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ θλῖψιν ἔχετε, ἀλλὰ θαρσεῖτε, ἐγὼ νενίκηκα τὸν κόσμον.

records.literal_gloss: These things I have spoken to you so that in me peace you may have; in the world affliction you have, but have courage, I have overcome the world."

en.L: These things I have spoken to you so that in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} you may have peace. In the world you have affliction; but have courage, I have overcome the world."
en.B: I have said these things to you so that you may have peace in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. In the world you have affliction. But have courage: I have overcome the world."
en.R: I have told you all this so that you can have peace in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. In the world you have trouble. But be brave! I have already won the victory over the world."

fr.L: Je vous ai dit ces choses afin qu’en {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} vous ayez la paix. Dans le monde, vous avez de la détresse ; mais ayez courage, j’ai vaincu le monde. »
fr.B: Je vous ai dit cela pour que vous ayez la paix en {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}. Dans le monde, vous connaissez la détresse. Mais ayez courage : j’ai vaincu le monde. »
fr.R: Je vous ai dit tout cela pour que vous ayez la paix en {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}. Dans le monde, vous avez à souffrir. Mais courage ! J’ai déjà remporté la victoire sur le monde. »

vi.L: Ta đã nói những điều này với các con để trong {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} các con có bình an. Trong thế gian các con có hoạn nạn; nhưng hãy can đảm lên, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã thắng thế gian."
vi.B: Ta đã nói với các con những điều này để các con có bình an trong {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Trong thế gian các con có hoạn nạn. Nhưng hãy vững lòng: {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã chiến thắng thế gian."
vi.R: Ta đã nói với các con mọi điều này để các con được bình an trong {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Trong thế gian các con gặp khó khăn. Nhưng hãy can đảm lên! Ta đã chiến thắng thế gian rồi."

ko.L: 내가 이것들을 너희에게 말한 것은 너희가 내 안에서 평안을 누리게 하려는 것이다. 세상에서는 너희가 환난을 당한다. 그러나 용기를 내라. 내가 세상을 이겼다."
ko.B: 내가 너희에게 이것을 말한 것은, 너희가 내 안에서 평안을 누리게 하려는 것이다. 세상에서 너희는 환난을 겪는다. 그러나 용기를 내라. 내가 세상을 이겼다."
ko.R: 내가 이 모든 말을 한 것은, 너희가 내 안에서 평안을 얻게 하려는 것이다. 세상에서 너희는 어려움을 겪는다. 그러나 힘을 내라! 내가 이미 세상을 이겼다."

decisions.choice: you have, present tense, as in the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts read "you will have"; the present is well attested in the earliest manuscripts. The present says that affliction is already part of life in the world for Jesus's followers, as 15:18-16:4 has described. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: affliction: pressure and distress, especially the hostility the disciples will meet
alternatives: the great tribulation at the end of the age
decisions.reason: The word means being pressed hard. In 16:21 it is the pain of a woman giving birth; in the farewell talk it is the hatred and persecution the world will bring (15:18-20; 16:2). It is not here a technical term for the end times.

decisions.choice: the world: humanity set against God, the source of the disciples' affliction
decisions.reason: "In me" and "in the world" are set side by side: peace in Jesus, affliction in the world. The world here is the world that hates Jesus and his disciples (15:18-19), whose ruler has been judged (16:11). World is a key term.

decisions.choice: I have overcome: a victory already won, spoken before the cross
decisions.reason: The verb is in the perfect tense, used of a completed act whose result stands. Jesus speaks on the eve of his death as one who has already won. The same verb is used of the believer's victory over the world, which comes through him (1 John 5:4-5). The "I" is emphatic.

decisions.choice: have courage (L, B); be brave (R)
decisions.reason: The verb means to be bold or confident in the face of danger. "Be of good cheer" now sounds like a call to be cheerful, which is not the point. "Have courage" says the sense in ordinary words; Readable says it more simply still.

decisions.choice: affliction (L, B), trouble (R); overcome (L, B), already won the victory over (R)
decisions.reason: "Tribulation" now suggests the end times to many readers (meaning decision m2); "affliction" keeps the sense of pressure from outside. "Overcome" is the word of 1 John 5:4-5 for the same verb. Readable adds "already" to bring out the perfect tense (meaning decision m4).

decisions.choice: la détresse (L, B); vous avez à souffrir (R)
decisions.reason: The word means pressure and distress, above all the hostility the disciples will meet (meaning decision m2). "Tribulations" is church language; "la détresse" is the plain word, used for the same noun in verse 21. Readable says what it means for them, keeping the present tense of the SBLGNT (m1).

decisions.choice: 평안 for "peace" (key term); 환난 (L, B), 어려움 (R) for "affliction"
decisions.reason: 평안 is the guide's key term for peace; 환난 is pressure and distress from without, and Readable uses the everyday 어려움.
